metrics.prompt: Review our implementation of context ofr inferrence in sketch/sketch7 and report how it functions. List any issues you see. Make recommendations on architectural improvements.

findings: Context assembly is orchestrated by `Builder.Build` (context.go:52), which combines static/dynamic `Sections` (system prompts) with a truncated conversation `Messages` transcript into a final `Payload`.

`Sections` are generated via `BuildSections` (sections.go:15) by iterating over agent `Projections`. It supports projection types: system, interaction, cognitive_state, workflow_state, binding, and repo_context, each producing structured system-role content.
Message history is reconstructed from `SessionHistory` records via `buildTranscript` (context.go:79). It maps user, assistant, tool call, and tool result records into a linear message slice.

Truncation via `trimMessages` (context.go:99) groups messages into blocks (keeping tool call/result pairs intact), selects the most recent blocks up to `maxMessages`, and forces inclusion of the latest user anchor to preserve context coherence.

Repository context is cached at the package level via a global `defaultRepoCache` (sections.go:13, repo.go:23). `RepoContextCache.Summary` (repo.go:29) avoids repeated filesystem walks and `git` subprocess invocations by respecting a `RefreshEveryTurns` threshold and checking historical snapshots.

Workflow progress tracking (`workflowProgress`, sections.go:86) hardcodes a state sequence (`intake`, `repo_orientation`, `clarification`, etc.) and scans session history to determine if prerequisites are met before allowing transitions.

Test coverage in `context_test.go` validates that truncation preserves the latest coherent user/assistant tail and respects tool call blocking, but does not test edge cases like empty history, single messages, or anchor injection logic.
unknowns: How `runner.Loop` consumes the `Payload` and maps it to the LLM provider's API (e.g., OpenAI messages format).
How `prompt.BuildProjectionPlan` determines projection ordering and calculates `maxHistory`.
Whether token-aware truncation is implemented elsewhere (e.g., in the provider or runner), since `trimMessages` relies solely on message counts.
How concurrent sessions are managed at the application level and whether the global cache causes contention or cross-session pollution.
Contents of `repo_test.go` and how repo context caching is validated under concurrent or multi-turn scenarios.
